Option 1: "حقّ ا که اگر از من سرگشته ترت افتد - گرعاشق روی خود سرگشته همی خواهی"

This seems to be about divine truth/righteousness (حق) and being "سرگشته" (distraught/perplexed). The meaning appears to be: "It's true that if you become distraught because of me, you would want the lover to be distraught by your face." This is about love, devotion, and perhaps the reciprocity of emotional states in love. It suggests a kind of mutual suffering or shared emotional experience.

Option 2: "کآتش اندر گنه آدم و حوا فکنم - از دل تنگ گنهکار برآرم آهی"

This mentions "آتش" (fire), "گنه آدم و حوا" (sin of Adam and Eve), "دل تنگ گنهکار" (sorrowful heart of a sinner), and "آه" (sigh). This is clearly about sin, repentance, and spiritual suffering. The speaker is expressing sorrow over the original sin and their own sins, sighing from a heavy heart.

Option 3: "مست خیزی مست باشی جاودان - مست بودی مست رفتی از جهان"

This is about being "مست" (intoxicated/rapt). It says: "You dance intoxicated, may you be intoxicated eternally - You were intoxicated, you left the world intoxicated." This celebrates a state of ecstatic intoxication, perhaps spiritual or mystical, as a permanent, desirable condition.

Option 4: "فتاده خشک لب بر شاهراهیم - اگر چه غرق دریای گناهیم"

This says: "We have fallen dry-lipped on the highway - although we are drowning in the sea of sin." This expresses being in a state of sin ("غرق دریای گناهیم" - drowning in the sea of sin) but also being desperate/dry-lipped on the path. It's about sin and spiritual desperation.
